ja: あのとき君が引っ越しを手伝ってくれていなかったら、僕は今でも段ボールに囲まれて暮らしていただろうね。
en: If you hadn't helped me move back then, I'd still be living surrounded by cardboard boxes.
alternatives: If you hadn't helped me with the move back then, I'd still be surrounded by cardboard boxes.
Without your help with the move back then, I'd still be living among cardboard boxes.
point: 過去の条件は had 過去分詞、今の結果は would be -ing

ja: 引っ越しの手伝いを頼んだら、兄は私にピザをおごらせてから、やっと引き受けてくれたんだ。
en: When I asked my brother to help me move, he made me buy him pizza before he finally agreed to help.
alternatives: When I asked my brother to help me move, he didn't agree until he'd made me buy him pizza.
My brother made me buy him pizza before he finally agreed to help me move.
point: 「〜させる」は make 人 + 動詞の原形（to は付けない）

ja: 田中さんは、来週なら喜んであなたの原稿に目を通すけど、今週は締め切りで手一杯だと言っていました。
en: Ms. Tanaka said she'd be happy to look over your draft next week, but that she was swamped with deadlines this week.
alternatives: Ms. Tanaka said she would gladly go over your draft next week, but that she had too many deadlines this week.
Mr. Tanaka said he'd be happy to look over your draft next week, but that he was swamped with deadlines this week.
point: 伝える側の過去に合わせて will → would、is → was

ja: 彼女は今週もう3回も僕のシフトを代わってくれたから、今回は僕が引き受けるべきだね。
en: She's already covered my shift three times this week, so I should take this one.
alternatives: She's already taken my shift three times this week, so I should do this one.
Since she's covered for me three times this week already, I ought to take this one.
point: 「今週もう3回」は現在完了、already の位置に注意

ja: もっと早く言ってくれていたら、引っ越しを喜んで手伝ったのに。
en: If you had told me earlier, I would have been happy to help you move.
alternatives: If you'd let me know sooner, I would've gladly helped you move.
If you'd told me sooner, I'd have been happy to help you move.
point: 過去の仮定は if + had 過去分詞、主節は would have 過去分詞

ja: 引っ越しの手伝い、何時に行けばいい？
en: What time should I come to help you move?
alternatives: When should I come to help you move?
What time should I come over to help with the move?
point: 「何時に」は What time で文頭に置く

ja: 紙をちょっともらえる？メモを取りたいんだ。
en: Can I have some paper? I need to take notes.
alternatives: Could I get some paper? I want to take notes.
Can you give me some paper? I need to write something down.
point: paper は数えられないので a paper ではなく some paper

ja: ご近所さんに猫の世話を頼んだこと、ある？私は先週初めてお隣の奥さんに頼んだんだけど、快く引き受けてくれたよ。
en: Have you ever asked a neighbor to look after your cat? I asked the woman next door for the first time last week, and she gladly agreed.
alternatives: Have you ever asked a neighbor to take care of your cat? Last week I asked the lady next door for the first time, and she was happy to do it.
Have you ever had a neighbor look after your cat? I asked the woman next door for the first time last week, and she was happy to help.
point: 経験は現在完了、last week があれば過去形

ja: 来週末の引っ越し、手伝ってもらえないかな？お昼はもちろんおごるから。
en: Could you help me out with the move next weekend? I'll buy you lunch, of course.
alternatives: Would you be able to help me out with the move next weekend? Lunch is on me, of course.
Could you give me a hand with the move next weekend? I'll treat you to lunch, of course.
point: 「手伝う」は help me out with 〜 の句動詞で自然に

ja: 彼女は週末に車を貸してくれただけでなく、鍵を渡す前にガソリンまで満タンにしてくれたんです。
en: Not only did she lend me her car for the weekend, but she also filled up the tank before handing me the keys.
alternatives: She not only lent me her car for the weekend but also filled up the tank before she handed me the keys.
Not only did she let me borrow her car for the weekend, she even filled the tank before giving me the keys.
point: Not only で始めたら did she lend と語順を倒置する

ja: ごめん、今料理してるんだ。あとで手伝うね。
en: Sorry, I'm cooking right now. I'll help later.
alternatives: Sorry, I'm in the middle of cooking. I'll help you later.
Sorry, I'm busy cooking. I'll help out later.
point: 「今〜してる」は I'm cooking と進行形にする

ja: 駅に着いたら電話するから、迎えに来てもらえる？
en: I'll call you when I get to the station. Could you come pick me up?
alternatives: I'll give you a call when I get to the station. Can you come get me?
Could you come pick me up? I'll call you once I get to the station.
point: 未来のことでも when 節は現在形で get to とする

ja: ごめん、今夜は君の犬の散歩を代わってあげられないんだ。
en: Sorry, I can't walk your dog for you tonight.
alternatives: Sorry, I can't take your dog for a walk tonight.
I'm sorry, I won't be able to walk your dog tonight.
point: 「散歩させる」は walk を他動詞で使い walk your dog とする

ja: 今、忙しい？ちょっとお願いがあるんだ。
en: Are you busy? I need a favor.
alternatives: Are you busy now? I have a favor to ask.
Are you busy right now? I need a favor.
point: 「忙しい？」は be 動詞で Are you busy? と聞く

ja: 私が引っかかったのは、頼まれたこと自体じゃなくて、まるで私に借りでもあるかのような彼の頼み方だったんだ。
en: What bothered me wasn't the favor itself, but the way he asked, as if I owed him one.
alternatives: It wasn't the favor itself that bothered me, but the way he asked, as if I owed him something.
What got to me wasn't the favor itself but how he asked, like I owed him one.
point: What bothered me wasn't A, but B で「引っかかったのは A ではなく B」を強調する

ja: 僕、土曜に友達の引っ越しの手伝いを頼まれてるんだ。
en: I've been asked to help my friend move on Saturday.
alternatives: I was asked to help my friend move on Saturday.
My friend asked me to help with their move on Saturday.
point: 「頼まれている」は受動態 have been asked to do で表す

ja: 先月彼女にカメラを貸したんだけど、まだ返してもらってないんだ。
en: I lent her my camera last month, but she hasn't given it back yet.
alternatives: I lent my camera to her last month, but she still hasn't returned it.
Last month I lent her my camera, and she hasn't returned it yet.
point: last month は過去形、まだ返っていない今の状態は現在完了

ja: ごめん、土曜は兄の結婚式に行くことになってるんだけど、日曜なら犬の世話をしてあげられるよ。
en: Sorry, I'm going to my brother's wedding on Saturday, but I could look after your dog on Sunday.
alternatives: Sorry, I'm attending my brother's wedding on Saturday, but I can take care of your dog on Sunday.
Sorry, I've got my brother's wedding on Saturday, but I could watch your dog on Sunday.
point: 決まっている予定は進行形 I'm going to my brother's wedding

ja: 忙しいなら無理に引き受けなくていいからね。気を遣わないで。
en: If you're busy, you don't have to take it on. Don't feel obligated.
alternatives: Don't worry about it if you're busy. You don't have to say yes.
If you're too busy, you don't need to do it. Don't feel pressured.
point: 「しなくていい」は don't have to、mustn't は禁止になる

ja: 店長にシフトを減らしてもらうよう頼んでもらえますか？正直、かなり困っているんです。
en: Could you ask the manager to cut my shifts? Honestly, I'm really struggling.
alternatives: Would you ask the manager to reduce my shifts? To be honest, I'm having a hard time.
Could you ask the manager to give me fewer shifts? Honestly, I'm really struggling.
point: 「人に〜するよう頼む」は ask + 人 + to do の語順
